content.text:
This page turned out to have far fewer structural defects than a typical case in this series (no custom widgets, no dialogs, no buttons to fix) — the two links were already real anchors that natively support Tab/Enter, and my contrast check on every text/background pair in the stylesheet already cleared 4.5:1. The real defects were structural/semantic:

**Defects found**
1. No landmark structure — the whole page was built from generic `<div>`s, so all content sat outside any landmark region (fails axe's `region`/`landmark-one-main` best-practice rules and hurts screen-reader navigation).
2. Focus indicator relied entirely on the browser default with no explicit style, so it wasn't guaranteed to be visible/consistent.
3. The two nav links jump to `#visit`/`#events`, but their targets (`<h1>`, `<div class="hours">`) weren't focusable, so keyboard/AT users following the link would have focus silently dropped to `<body>` instead of landing at the new content.

**Fixes applied**
- Changed `.top` → `<header>`, wrapped the two links in a `<nav aria-label="Primary">`, wrapped the hero + hours content in `<main>`, and changed `.bottom` → `<footer>`. This gives the page real landmarks without touching any visible layout (all styling stayed on the same classes/ids).
- Added `tabindex="-1"` to the `#visit` and `#events` targets so activating the in-page links moves focus to the destination for keyboard and screen-reader users, matching the mouse/visual behavior, without adding them to the normal Tab order.
- Added an explicit `a:focus-visible` outline (dark green, 2px, offset) so the focus indicator is guaranteed visible and matches the site's palette instead of relying on an unstyled default.

**Left alone**
- Both `data-track` attributes, both `id`s, and the instrumentation script — untouched.
- All visible text, colors, and layout — unchanged (contrast on every existing text/background pair already meets 4.5:1+, so no palette changes were needed).
- No custom widgets or dialogs exist on this page, so those parts of the contract (focus trapping, arrow-key patterns, inert background) don't apply here.

The two links are native `<a href>` elements, so Enter-to-activate and Tab reachability were already correct and needed no retrofitting.
